Extract outlier information from a Persephone object

Source: R/get_functions.R
getOutliers.Rd

This function retrieves outlier details (AO, LS, TC) from a fitted Persephone model, including coefficients, standard errors, t-statistics, and p-values. It processes the raw output from X-13ARIMA-SEATS or TRAMO/SEATS into a clean data frame with formatted dates and names.

Usage

getOutliers(x)

Arguments

x

A Persephone object (e.g., x13Single or tramoseatsSingle) with completed model run

Value

A data frame with columns:

name

Formatted outlier name (e.g., "AO1953.7" for additive outlier)

type

Outlier type: AO (Additive Outlier), LS (Level Shift), or TC (Transient Change)

coef.value

Estimated coefficient value

stde

Standard error of the coefficient (NA if coef.type is "FIXED")

t

T-statistic, coef.value / stde

crit.value

Critical value of the outlier test applied by JDemetra+: the value from the outlier specification if positive (x13: per outlier type, falling back to defva), otherwise the threshold computed internally (see Details)

pvalue

Two-sided p-value of t under a t distribution with neffectiveobs - nparams degrees of freedom

date

Date of the outlier as Date object

coef.type

Type of coefficient (usually "ESTIMATED")

autoout

Logical, TRUE for outliers detected automatically by X-13ARIMA-SEATS or TRAMO/SEATS, FALSE for outliers that were specified manually with the outliers argument

recentout

Logical, TRUE if the outlier falls into one of the last observations of the series: the last 5 observations for monthly series, the last 3 for quarterly series, the last 1 for all other frequencies (e.g., annual). Outliers before the beginning of the series or before the estimation span are never flagged.

Details

X-13ARIMA-SEATS and TRAMO/SEATS do not directly report standard errors, t-statistics, or p-values for outlier effects. These quantities are computed here from the estimated coefficients and the covariance matrix (bvar), following the same methodology as rjd3toolkit. Results can therefore be verified against summary(x$output$preprocessing)$xregs.

Because outliers are selected only when their absolute t-statistic exceeds the critical value defined in the outlier specification, the reported p-values are subject to selection effects. They should be viewed as descriptive statistics for the fitted model rather than as formal evidence of adjustment quality.

The output of a run does not distinguish manually specified from automatically detected outliers. autoout therefore compares the type/date pairs of the run output with the manually specified outliers read from the model specification (regarima$regression$outliers for x13, tramo$regression$outliers for tramoseats). recentout is evaluated independently of autoout, so a manually specified outlier close to the end of the series is flagged as well.

If the outlier specification defines no critical value, JDemetra+ computes one internally from the number of observations n of the estimation domain: x13 uses max(advancedComputer(0.05)(n), 2.8), an extreme-value approximation for the 95% quantile of the maximum of n standard normal variables; tramoseats uses max(simpleComputer()(n), 2), i.e. 3.3 up to 50 observations, rising by 0.0025 per observation up to 4.3. Both formulas are reproduced in calcOutlierCrit() and verified against the jdplus implementation. Note that during automatic model identification the engines may lower this value once (by about 14% for x13 and 12% for tramoseats); that reduction is not reported in the run output and is therefore not reflected in crit.value.

Note

This is an internal function used by other get* functions and diagnostics.

Examples

# obj <- perX13(AirPassengers, "rsa3", outliers = "AO1960.5")
# obj$run()
# getOutliers(obj)                  # all outliers
# subset(getOutliers(obj), autoout) # without the manually specified one
